name: Apple UIKit-Inspired Terminal CLI Design System
scope: CLI and optional keyboard-driven terminal UI only. No web interface.

paletteProvenance.attributionNote: Original UIKit palette and semantic tokens preserved as reference; terminal theme roles and rules authored as pragmatic adaptations, not official Apple terminal design standards.

light.notes: Semantic text/status hues may be darkened or lightened for legibility in a terminal; the untouched source palette is under appleUIKitReference. Transparent UIKit colors are not directly emitted as ANSI colors.

dark.notes: Semantic text/status hues may be darkened or lightened for legibility in a terminal; the untouched source palette is under appleUIKitReference. Transparent UIKit colors are not directly emitted as ANSI colors.

ansiStyleTokens.strong: SGR bold 1 when available; otherwise plain
ansiStyleTokens.secondary: Prefer semantic textSecondary color; use dim SGR 2 only for noncritical content
ansiStyleTokens.focus: reverse SGR 7 or selection background plus a visible > marker
ansiStyleTokens.underline: SGR 4 only for actionable/important short fragments; not decorative
ansiStyleTokens.plainTextFallback: No escape codes; print labels and structural whitespace

scope.target: Terminal-only command-line application (CLI); optional full-screen interactive terminal UI (TUI).
mustUse: terminal escape sequences only when supported
scope.principle: The CLI must remain usable without color, Unicode box drawing, a mouse, or an interactive terminal.

designPhilosophy: Clarity before decoration. A CLI is an interface for reading, composing, automating, and acting, not a tiny website.
Progressive disclosure: show the result first, then the next useful action; keep advanced data behind --verbose or --json.
Use semantic meaning, alignment, concise words, and predictable conventions instead of ornamental borders and large banners.
Respect system terminal theme and contrast; never force Apple-style white panels or glass effects.
Optimized for real workflows: pipeability, predictable exit codes, idempotence when possible, and useful diagnostics.

typography.fontPolicy: Do not control the terminal font. User chooses terminal font and size. Prefer readable monospace output; Fira Code is optional, not a prerequisite.

hierarchy.primaryTitle: Short sentence in bold if ANSI is enabled; plain text in non-TTY.
hierarchy.sectionHeading: One short heading, separated by a blank line only when helpful.
hierarchy.body: Normal intensity; prefer short lines and plain language.
hierarchy.metadata: Secondary color or dim, but never make actionable information illegible.
hierarchy.commands: Use shell-copyable literals without smart quotes; highlight the executable/flags only if supported.
hierarchy.numbers: Align right in tables; use tabular columns; keep units explicit.

avoid: font-dependent special ligatures as semantic indicators

layout.measure: Calculate terminal width at runtime for interactive screens; never assume 80 or 120 columns.
widthRules: Keep default success/output concise and scannable; favor natural wrapping over hard 80-column truncation.
If width is below about 60 columns, render a vertical key-value list instead of a wide table.
Never hide critical content through ellipsis; use explicit --full or --verbose for long values.
Truncate only supplementary text in interactive views, with a visible indicator.
Measure display width by terminal cells, not string length; combine, wide CJK characters, and ANSI codes need correct handling.
Use stable table widths within one render. Never use ANSI cursor tricks in piped output.
visualRhythm: One main output region per command.
One or two indentation levels at most.
Borders and cards are optional, restrained, and only for separation when needed.

color.source: Apple UIKit system palettes transcribed from Innei/apple-uikit-colors. Terminal roles under terminalThemes are authored adaptations.

usage.primaryText: Primary message, essential values, core command output.
usage.accent: Active menu item, current selection, links only when the terminal supports interaction.
usage.warning: Recoverable concerns with explicit WARNING prefix.
usage.error: Errors with explicit ERROR prefix and next action.
usage.focus: Active input indicator, always accompanied by shape/cursor/label.

rules: Prefer default foreground/background when terminal theme is unknown; do not assume light or dark.
Color is an enhancement: semantic text and symbols must convey state without color.
Never place a bright UIKit success green or yellow directly on white as tiny text without checking contrast.
For a known light/dark theme, use terminalThemes semantic roles rather than source swatches directly.
Avoid painting entire screen backgrounds in ordinary CLI output; enable themed backgrounds only in a deliberately full-screen TUI.
Avoid transparency, backdrop blur, and Liquid Glass: terminal cells do not support these concepts.
Colorize only TTY output by default; honor NO_COLOR, a --no-color flag, and an explicit --color=always override.

detectionOrder: If --no-color or NO_COLOR is set, disable ANSI colors.
If output stream is not a TTY, use plain text unless --color=always is explicitly requested.
If TERM is missing or dumb, do not emit ANSI control sequences.
If supported, use 24-bit truecolor; else 256 colors; else ANSI 16; else monochrome.

colorDepths.truecolor: Use SGR 38;2;R;G;B for foreground; 48;2;R;G;B for background. Finish styling with SGR reset.
colorDepths.ansi256: Approximate RGB against the xterm-256 palette; do not assume exact UIKit reproduction.
colorDepths.ansi16: Use readable, semantic roles and default terminal colors; do not presume standard hues/brightness.
colorDepths.none: Use labels, brackets, prefixes and indentation, not color.

hints.ttyCheck: isatty(stdout) and isatty(stdin) as appropriate; check the output stream actually being colored

terminalCapabilities.important: Environment variables are heuristics, not perfect detection. Prefer user flags or reliable capability libraries; terminal 16-color slots may be customized.

cliContract.naming: Lowercase kebab-case commands and long flags; short flags only for frequent actions.
help: app --help gives a brief overview, useful examples, command list, and conventions.
app COMMAND --help gives purpose, syntax, required inputs, flags, examples, and exit statuses.
Usage errors should propose the closest valid option, without flooding suggestions.

outputStreams.stdout: Requested machine-consumable result or the main human-readable result.
outputStreams.stderr: Diagnostics, progress, warnings, prompts, and failures; keep stdout clean for piping.
outputStreams.json: --json emits valid machine-readable JSON, without banners, colors, spinners, or explanatory text.
outputStreams.quiet: --quiet hides nonessential chatter without losing requested data or critical error messages.

exitCodes.130: Interrupted via Ctrl+C (conventional; platform-specific handling may vary)

nonInteractive: Detect non-TTY stdin/out and do not ask interactive questions; require arguments or fail with actionable usage.
Allow --yes / --force for carefully scoped confirmations; do not silently skip destructive checks.
Favor deterministic outputs for scripts and testing.
Avoid escape codes, animation, and interactive cursor control in pipes, logs, and CI.

interactiveTUI.whenToUse: Only when selecting or inspecting complex collections is substantially easier than flags and pipes. Every essential action must have a non-interactive CLI equivalent.

keyboard.up/down or j/k: Navigate lists where appropriate; show hints.
keyboard.space: Toggle a clearly labeled checkbox selection.
keyboard.escape: Close a dialog or back out one level.
keyboard.ctrl-c: Cancel or exit safely, restore terminal state.
keyboard.? or h: Open keyboard help without hijacking text input.
keyboard./: Search/filter when relevant; display active query.

interactiveTUI.focus: One obvious focus at a time. Combine highlight, prefix cursor (e.g. >), and explicit selected/checked status.
rendering: Use alternate screen only for a full-screen TUI; never for ordinary command output.
Diff-render changes when practical to reduce flicker and unnecessary redraws.
Adapt to terminal resize and very small dimensions; show a fallback if the interface cannot fit.
Always restore cursor visibility, terminal modes, alternate-screen state, and raw mode on exit or signal.
Do not require a mouse or clickable links.

commandResult.format: Primary answer first, details second, optional next step last.
commandResult.example:
Created 12 records.
Run `app records list` to inspect them.

warning.example: WARNING  2 entries were skipped because they have no ID.

error.example:
ERROR  Could not open config.json
Reason: Permission denied.
Try: Check file permissions or pass --config PATH.

progress.tty: One in-place concise progress line, with count and elapsed only if meaningful.
progress.nonTty: No spinner. For long tasks, write infrequent meaningful milestones to stderr.

table.useFor: Several records with concise, comparable attributes.
rules: Left-align text and right-align numeric values.
Do not put multi-paragraph content into cells.
Use vertical key-value view on narrow terminals.

list.useFor: Navigation, search results, short action choices.

rules: State requested value and default explicitly.
Support Enter to accept safe defaults.
Validate inline and preserve input after errors.
For secrets, disable input echo and never log values.

confirmation.format: Delete 12 records? This cannot be undone. [y/N]

emptyState.format: No <items> found. <Concrete action or next command>.
emptyState.example: No workspaces found. Create one with `app workspace create NAME`.

help.format: Purpose -> Usage -> Options -> Examples -> Related commands.
help.rule: Keep default --help short enough to scan without a pager.

notifications.rule: No toast UI: place a concise event in stderr; avoid breaking cursor or overwriting output.

accessibility: Never use color as the only status indicator; pair with text such as OK, WARNING, ERROR.
Do not assume Unicode glyphs have fixed width; offer ASCII-friendly characters and NO_COLOR.
Ensure important foreground roles have at least 4.5:1 contrast on documented backgrounds for truecolor themes.
Avoid fast blinking, animated flourishes, aggressive redraws, and inescapable interactions.
Support keyboard-only use; user can always reach Help and Exit.
Keep critical information out of dim-only text and never hide secrets behind merely colored text.
Respect plain-text screen readers and piping: avoid ASCII art, cursor-motion output, and misleading control codes.
securityAndReliability: Do not print API keys, access tokens, passwords, or sensitive env vars; mask secrets in verbose logs and errors.
Use safe defaults, confirmation for destructive actions, and explicit --force or --yes automation paths.
Treat terminal output from external processes/user content as untrusted; neutralize control characters to prevent escape injection.
Handle Ctrl+C, SIGTERM, and exceptions with cleanup, especially raw keyboard mode and cursor state.
Ensure stable exit codes and structured --json output for tooling integration.
Avoid hyperlink escape sequences or clipboard escape sequences unless explicitly supported and consented to.
qualityChecklist: A user can run --help and complete a typical task with no documentation.
The command works with NO_COLOR=1 and TERM=dumb.
Piped stdout is clean and valid; --json parses without stripping terminal escapes.
Error text describes cause and recovery, with nonzero exit code.
Key actions have flags/args even if there is an interactive menu.
The UI remains understandable at 40, 60, and 120 terminal columns.
Works in light, dark, 16-color, 256-color, truecolor, and monochrome contexts.
Terminal is fully restored after Ctrl+C and unexpected errors.
No web, React, CSS, browser UI, glassmorphism, or hover-based controls appear.
Numeric columns align; wrapped text does not break table layout.
All status states are legible even when colors are disabled.
